questions.question: For a random variable $X$ with CDF $F$, which probability does the survivor function $\overline F(x)=1-F(x)$ give?
A random variable $X$ has survivor function $\overline F$ with $\overline F(4)=0.3$. Which statement must hold?
Which continuity property holds for every survivor function $\overline F$?
options: It is right-continuous at every $x$, like the CDF $F$.
It is left-continuous at every $x$, since $1-F$ reverses $F$.
It is continuous at every $x$, with no jumps at all.
It is right-continuous only when $X$ is a continuous variable.

questions.question: A machine's lifetime $T$ satisfies $\mathbb P(T\le100)=0.2$, with time measured in hours. Which statement follows?
options: The machine has probability $0.2$ of working beyond 100 hours.
The machine has probability $0.8$ of failing by 100 hours.
The machine has expected remaining lifetime 80 hours at time 100.
The machine has probability $0.8$ of working beyond 100 hours.

questions.question: For a continuous random variable $X$ with density $f$, how does $\mathbb P(X\ge x)$ compare with $\overline F(x)$?
options: $\mathbb P(X\ge x)=\overline F(x)+f(x)$, adding the density at $x$
$\mathbb P(X\ge x)>\overline F(x)$ at every $x$ in the support
$\mathbb P(X\ge x)=1-\overline F(x)$, the complementary event

questions.question: For $X\sim\operatorname{Exp}(2)$, what is $\overline F(1.5)$?
For $X\sim\operatorname{Bern}(0.7)$, what are $\overline F(1)$ and $\mathbb P(X\ge1)$?
A waiting time $X$ has exponential distribution with rate 2, so $X\ge0$ almost surely. What is $\overline F(-1)$?
For $X\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,10)$, what is $\overline F(x)$ for $0\le x\le10$?
With which probability does a waiting time $X\sim\operatorname{Exp}(1)$ end in the interval $(1,2]$?
A random variable $X$ has survivor function $\overline F$. At a real number $a$, its left limit is $\overline F(a-)=0.65$ and its value is $\overline F(a)=0.40$. Which statement follows?
A nonnegative continuous lifetime $T$ has survivor function $\overline F(s)>0$ for every $s\ge0$ and is memoryless: $\mathbb P(T>s+t\mid T>s)=\mathbb P(T>t)$ for $s,t\ge0$. What does this imply?
A random variable $X$ has density $f$ and survivor function $\overline F$. At a point $x$ where $f$ is continuous, how is $f(x)$ obtained from $\overline F$?
A bulb's lifetime $T$ in hours is $\operatorname{Exp}(0.5)$. What is $\mathbb P(T>5\mid T>3)$?
Three independent components with $\operatorname{Exp}(1)$ lifetimes are connected in series, so the system fails at the first component failure. What is the system's survivor function at $t\ge0$?
For $G\sim\operatorname{Geo}(p)$ counting failures before the first success, let $0<p<1$ and $\mathbb P(G\ge m)=(1-p)^m$ for integers $m\ge0$. What is $\overline F(n)$ for an integer $n\ge1$?
Each function below equals $1$ for $x<0$; its values for $x\ge0$ are given. Which one cannot be the survivor function of a real-valued random variable?

An integrable real-valued random variable $X$ has survivor function $\overline F$. Define $A=\int_0^\infty\overline F(t)\,\mathrm{d}t$ and $B=\int_{-\infty}^0[1-\overline F(t)]\,\mathrm{d}t$. Which expression gives $\mathbb E X$?

Two independent components with lifetimes $\operatorname{Exp}(1)$ and $\operatorname{Exp}(2)$ work in parallel, so the system works while at least one does. What is the system's survivor function for $t\ge0$?
A random variable $X$ has $\mathbb P(X=1)=0.2$, $\mathbb P(X=2)=0.5$ and $\mathbb P(X=3)=0.3$. What is $\int_0^\infty\overline F(t)\,\mathrm{d}t$?
